why: B drove every routable path against real Router (31 live requests) and that is how it found two defects A's simulator-only run missed — a function result sent without its originating call (400) and a streamed tool call abandoned on Router's leading chunk (empty replies) — then fixed both in shapes the provider also accepts, so the bot's headline plugin feature survives the move; A ships the same one-line wrap but asserts 'the legacy functions/function_call payload translates cleanly' and 'loses: nothing', a claim B's evidence falsifies, which means A's migration would silently break tool use and poison the in-memory history for every later turn. A's system-level thinking is in places sharper (the N_CHOICES/presence_penalty coverage trap, the Responses-native port, a per-chat cache key in code rather than per-feature), but B's improvement set is live-verified, correctly ranked, and honest about what Router cannot give gpt-4o — I would ship B and act on A's two extra items as follow-ups.
A_best: Spotting that N_CHOICES>1 or a non-zero PRESENCE_PENALTY makes the runtime keep every chat request on the provider with no error, so a deployment's whole chat volume can silently leave the gateway — a coverage fragility B never notices — plus the honest i6 framing that the shape kept is a 2023 Chat Completions call while every Router lever lives on Responses.
B_best: Finding and fixing, against real Router, the two Responses-strictness breaks in the plugin loop (missing assistant function_call message, stream search ending on the first chunk) including the matching __count_tokens update, with before/after live evidence — the difference between a migration that works and one that looks like it works.
A_worst: Zero live requests and a false 'nothing lost': the function-call evidence line claims the legacy payload translates cleanly when it actually 400s, so the migration's central behaviour-preservation claim is wrong; smaller errors follow (summarisation called a per-turn tax when it fires on overflow, and cheap fallbacks sold as a benefit on a user-facing reply).
B_worst: Settling for a per-feature prompt_cache_key in the built branch and deferring the per-chat key — the version that actually earns the provider affinity and cache hits — to an unbuilt proposal, and leaving unexamined whether provider_timeout is truly only an idle-gap timer, which its 'loses: nothing' depends on.
